B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP access price was found. MCP actions can create billable resources: project and branch creation have cost checks and confirmation flows. Branching requires a paid plan.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing lists Free at $0/month, Pro from $25/month, Team from $599/month, and Enterprise at custom pricing. Additional projects and usage can add charges.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Supabase plan and usage charges apply to resources and services used through MCP. The server's cost workflow covers create_project and create_branch; a zero-cost project quote does not prompt for confirmation.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth sign-in grants a client access to an organization. Available tools vary by project scope, feature groups, read-only mode, permissions, client elicitation support, and plan-dependent branching. Hosted configuration supports project_ref, read_only, features, and skip_elicitations. Organization SSO and administrator authorization apply to enterprise-managed authorization.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization administrator; users select project scope, read-only mode, feature groups, and confirmation-skip settings in the connection URL or configuration panel.

The metadata advertises bearer tokens in headers, authorization server https://api.supabase.com, resource name “Supabase MCP (Beta)”, and resource documentation https://mcp.supabase.com/api/mcp. The protected-resource document's raw scopes_supported are organizations:read, projects:read, projects:write, database:write, database:read, analytics:read, secrets:read, edge_functions:read, edge_functions:write, environment:read, environment:write, storage:read, storage:write. Authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code, refresh_token, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer; registration_endpoint https://api.supabase.com/platform/oauth/apps/register; PKCE methods S256 and plain; token auth client_secret_basic and client_secret_post. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Read/write tools are distinguished in code annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint); read-only mode excludes or adapts write tools. 2. Cost and destructive-SQL confirmation are server elicitations where supported; confirmation may be skipped by URL parameter, while client call approval is a separate client control. SQL detection is a guardrail, not a guarantee. 3. OAuth scopes are in the metadata above; docs map tools to PAT permissions and say access is limited by granted permissions. Enterprise-managed OAuth requires SSO and organization owner/admin client authorization; token lifetime/revocation details were not found. 4. Hosted modes include project scoping, read-only, feature-group selection, and skip_elicitations. Storage is disabled by default per docs; branching requires a paid plan. Local CLI and self-hosted endpoints are separate variants. 5. Database RLS remains enforced; project scoping narrows accessible resources. Secret values are entered in the Dashboard rather than chat or tool arguments. Tool results may contain untrusted user data and code wraps SQL results with warnings. 6. query_logs permits up to 24 hours per request; repository notebook results cap at about 1 MB. Cost can accrue for projects and branches. 7. Schemas validate inputs; transport validates query options and rejects invalid skip_elicitations names. Project IDs are injected in scoped mode and omitted from schemas. No evidence of operator defaults overriding supplied tool arguments was found. 8. Monitoring/audit trail and MCP-specific telemetry disclosure were not found in reviewed docs. 9. Code defines submit_feedback/delete_feedback; submission instructions say use on user request or bug/missing capability, ask before unsolicited feedback, exclude sensitive content, and show the deletion token. These names are absent from hosted docs list. No upsell message found. 10. Initialize instructions and tool descriptions steer agent behavior; code instructs installing Supabase agent skills separately. 11. No evidence that past agent behavior changes future outputs or tools. 12. Hosted global endpoint, CLI local endpoint, and self-hosted server are documented variants; no nested sub-server architecture found. 13. execute_sql is a raw SQL escape hatch; run_notebook also runs SQL cells. Their access remains subject to authentication, permissions, and read-only mode.

Counting grouped names gives 33; the official feature page says “over 20 tools” without an exact total. The pinned official repository defines 40 tools. Seven code-defined tools absent from the hosted docs list are get_logs, submit_feedback, delete_feedback, create_notebook, list_notebooks, get_notebook, and run_notebook; treated as local-equivalent definitions with hosted availability Unknown. No catalogue-only tools were added. Claude's third-party connector page reports “Show all 32 tools” and lists a differing set, including get_logs; its count/list differs from the hosted docs and code. Feature settings, project scope, server support, and permissions change the available count.

E_aggregated.token_method: The repository contains definitions and initialize instructions, but no serialized endpoint tools/list response was available to count characters. The token count for the endpoint context was not determinable from the collected evidence.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Product UI/API supports operations beyond this published MCP list, including managing organization members, invitations, webhooks, OAuth apps, and broader platform settings. The personal access token documentation lists MCP tools and permissions separately from many Management API operations. The hosted MCP tool list does not document these operations as available through MCP.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs recommend project scoping, read-only mode, narrow queries, manual client approval, review of outputs, and avoiding production data unless required. These recommendations depend partly on client configuration and user choices. Verbatim: “Keep manual approval enabled for interactive work, and review each tool call before you run it.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: Docs state database-level RLS remains enforced; project scope limits resources; read-only mode uses a read-only Postgres user. Secret values are entered through the Dashboard, not chat or tool arguments. Docs caution that SQL result wrapping is “not foolproof”.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: For supported cost elicitation, creation pauses for user approval, cost is checked again before creation, and declining or expiring creates nothing. Destructive-SQL confirmation applies only when detection and client form support are present.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Project scoping, read-only behavior, input validation, and tool gating have implementation support in public code. Elicitation handling is implemented but conditional on client capability/configuration; docs explicitly say SQL detection can miss destructive statements and elicitation is not proof of human approval. Advice to manually review actions is a client/user practice rather than an enforced server check.

contradictions: OAuth protected-resource metadata labels the endpoint “Supabase MCP (Beta)”, while the vendor feature page lists MCP Server stage as “General Availability”.

The hosted docs say all feature groups except Storage are enabled by default. The pinned public implementation's DEFAULT_FEATURES excludes both Storage and Notebooks; the docs do not name Notebooks in their group list. Repository and hosted deployment defaults may differ.

The official repository contains get_logs and four notebook tools plus submit_feedback and delete_feedback, which are absent from the hosted docs tool list. Hosted availability is not established by the public code.

Claude's third-party connector directory reports 32 tools and includes get_logs, while the official hosted docs name 33 grouped tools and the public code defines 40. Catalogue tool names/counts do not match the docs/code inventory.

The resource metadata advertises broad read/write scopes, while hosted docs say manual OAuth app setup should grant write access to all available scopes because finer-grained scopes are not yet supported; the metadata enumerates separate capability scopes. Whether each endpoint tool maps to a corresponding runtime scope was not found.
observations_for_research: Tool availability can be configured through URL parameters that change the server's listed surface, including project scope, read-only mode, feature groups, and selected elicitation skips.
Some confirmation flows are server-side tool-call pauses, but collection and display depend on client elicitation support; the legacy cost workflow instead uses tools and agent-facing descriptions.
The public implementation includes an explicit feedback submission/deletion pair with an agent instruction to ask before unsolicited submission and provide a deletion token.
Tool descriptions and server initialize instructions carry behavior guidance, including sequencing suggestions and warnings about untrusted database content.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/, and code/ before other sources. The official docs tool list and official repository were reviewed; the repo is pinned to the supplied latest commit. The repository represents the product's public implementation and CLI/local usage, but exact hosted deployment equivalence and endpoint tool listing were not independently verified. OAuth metadata was supplied as pre-fetched evidence; the origin-level protected-resource URL and OpenID configuration returned 404. Pricing page used as current vendor pricing; MCP-specific charge not stated. MCP-specific privacy retention, AI-training, telemetry, and endpoint audit details were not found in reviewed docs. Unofficial/community server listings were excluded from evidence.
